subject: English
text: Who first discovered Lencho's letter to God and brought it to the postmaster?
explanation: A postman, who was also an employee at the post office, found the letter addressed 'To God' and showed it to his boss.

options.text: A postman of the post office

subject: English
text: On which day did Nelson Mandela take the oath as the first black president of South Africa?
explanation: Mandela was sworn in on 10th May 1994, during the inauguration ceremony held at the Union Buildings amphitheatre in Pretoria.

subject: English
text: What was Tricki's main problem according to Dr. Herriot in 'A Triumph of Surgery'?
explanation: Tricki's only fault was greed. He had never been known to refuse food and would tackle a meal at any hour.

subject: English
text: In Leslie Norris's poem 'A Tiger in the Zoo', how are the tiger's eyes described?
explanation: The poet describes the tiger as staring with his 'brilliant eyes' at the 'brilliant stars' in the night.

subject: English
text: What was the age of Anil in the story 'The Thief's Story'?
explanation: Anil was a tall, lean fellow of about twenty-five years, who lived a simple life writing for magazines.

subject: English
text: Fill in the blank with the correct determiner: ________ of the two candidates is qualified for the post.
explanation: 'Neither' is used to refer to 'not one nor the other' of two things or people, and takes a singular verb.

subject: English
text: In 'From the Diary of Anne Frank', who was the only member of the Frank family to survive World War II?
explanation: Anne's father, Otto Frank, was the only survivor of the family who later published Anne's diary.

subject: English
text: In 'The Black Aeroplane', how did the narrator behave inside the storm clouds when he saw the mysterious plane?
explanation: The narrator was glad to see another person and followed the strange black aeroplane like an obedient child.

options.text: He followed the other plane like an obedient child.
He turned back and flew towards Paris.
He tried to overtake the black plane.
He called the security radar for assistance.

subject: English
text: In the poem 'How to Tell Wild Animals', what is the Bengal Tiger's distinguishing feature?
explanation: The Bengal Tiger is described as a noble wild beast with black stripes on a yellow background (ground).

options.text: Black stripes on a yellow ground
A large mane around his neck
Spots similar to a leopard's coat
A tail that winds around tree branches

subject: English
text: Choose the correct indirect form of: The doctor said to me, 'Don't eat junk food.'
explanation: Negative imperatives in indirect speech change the reporting verb to 'advised' and use 'not to + verb'.

options.text: The doctor advised me not to eat junk food.
The doctor advised me to don't eat junk food.
The doctor ordered me that I do not eat junk food.
The doctor suggested me to not eating junk food.

subject: English
text: What physical description of Ausable is given in 'The Midnight Visitor'?
explanation: Ausable was a secret agent who did not fit any description of a spy, being very fat and sloppy.

options.text: Old, frail, and wearing thick glasses

subject: English
text: In 'Madam Rides the Bus', why did Valli stand up on her seat during the bus ride?
explanation: Valli stood up because the canvas blind covering the lower part of the bus window blocked her view of the outside landscape.

options.text: Because the window blind cut off her view outside.
Because the conductor asked her to stand up.
Because she wanted to get off the bus early.
Because she was excited to see the canal water.

subject: English
text: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb: The novelist and the dramatist ________ arrived.
explanation: The repetition of the article 'the' before both nouns shows they refer to two distinct people. Therefore, the verb must be plural ('have').

subject: English
text: In 'A Question of Trust', which house did Horace Danby plan to rob after studying its layout for two weeks?
explanation: Horace planned to rob the safe containing fifteen thousand pounds worth of jewels at Shotover Grange.

subject: English
text: In 'The Ball Poem', what does the phrase 'in the world of possessions' mean?
explanation: It refers to the materialist world where people love to own, buy, and accumulate material possessions.

options.text: A world where material things are highly valued and owned.
A world of spiritual and religious beliefs.
A world where toys are distributed for free.
A world dominated by science and technology.

subject: English
text: What critical discovery did Richard Ebright make regarding the gold spots on monarch butterfly pupae?
explanation: Ebright proved that the spots were not decorative but produced a hormone necessary for the butterfly's development.

options.text: The spots produce a hormone necessary for the butterfly's development.
The spots are purely decorative to attract mates.
The spots are used to absorb heat from sunlight.
The spots serve as a camouflage mechanism against predators.

subject: English
text: Fill in the blank with the appropriate modal verb: You ________ pay your taxes on time as it is a legal duty.
explanation: 'Must' is used to express logical necessity or legal requirement, which fits the context of tax payments.

subject: English
text: In 'The Necklace', what truth did Madame Forestier reveal to Matilda ten years after the ball?
explanation: Madame Forestier revealed that her original necklace was not real diamonds but cheap imitation jewelry worth only five hundred francs.

options.text: Her original necklace was fake and made of imitation diamonds.
She had sold the necklace to buy a new house.
She had found the lost necklace in her wardrobe.
The necklace was a gift from M. Loisel's family.

subject: English
text: In 'The Proposal', what was Chubukov's primary social class or occupation?
explanation: Stephen Stepanovitch Chubukov was a wealthy Russian landowner and neighbor of Lomov.

subject: English
text: In the poem 'Amanda!', what is Amanda's mother correcting when she says: 'Stop that slouching and sit up straight!'?
explanation: Her mother is correcting Amanda's lazy sitting posture (slouching) to make her sit upright.

options.text: Her reading habits in the dark
Her way of speaking to elders

subject: English
text: Why did Bholi develop a stammering problem during her childhood?
explanation: Bholi fell off her cot in infancy, damaging her brain. Later, when she started speaking at age five, other children mimicked and teased her, making her lose confidence and stammer.

options.text: She suffered brain damage in infancy and was teased by other children.
She was born mute and could not speak at all.
She had a severe case of smallpox that damaged her tongue.
Her mother kept her isolated from other children.

subject: English
text: In 'Glimpses of India', what is the traditional dress of the Coorgis called, and what does it resemble?
explanation: The traditional black coat with an embroidered waistbelt is called 'Kuppia', which resembles the 'Kuffia' worn by Arabs.

options.text: Kuppia, which resembles the Kuffia worn by Arabs.
Kabai, which resembles the frocks worn by bakers.
Lungi, which resembles traditional south Indian dress.
Dhoti, which resembles north Indian formal dress.

subject: English
text: Choose the correct indirect form of: She said, 'Alas! I have lost my purse.'
explanation: Exclamatory sentences expressing sorrow use 'exclaimed with sorrow' or 'exclaimed sadly', and the tense shifts to past perfect.

options.text: She exclaimed with sorrow that she had lost her purse.
She said sadly that I have lost my purse.
She cried that she lost her purse.
She exclaimed with sorrow that she has lost her purse.

subject: English
text: In 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon', Belinda's other pets mocked Custard by comparing him to which legendary figure?
explanation: Ink, Blink, and Mustard rudely called Custard 'Percival', referring to a legendary knight of King Arthur who was mocked for his cowardice.

subject: English
text: In 'The Book That Saved the Earth', what alternative purpose does Noodle suggest for the 'sandwiches' (books) in the library?
explanation: Noodle suggests that Earthlings do not eat them but use them as devices for eye communication (reading).

options.text: Decoy items to hide Martian weapons.
